title: Reject an export with six planted defects

blocks.text: A fictional utility's planning database sends its portfolio export to CIPT Lite as text: one row per project and one per yearly budget, every cell a string, the way `csv.DictReader` hands them over. This cycle's export has six defects planted in it. Your reader must refuse it, find all six, and accept a clean export as the snapshot every later milestone uses.

**The rows.** `export["projects"]` holds rows with the columns `id`, `program`, `region`, `cost` (the yearly amounts in $k joined by `;`), `earliest`, `latest`, `must` (`"0"` or `"1"`), `parent` (an id, or `""`), `lag`, `group` (an alternative group, or `""`) and `crews`. `export["budgets"]` holds `year` and `amount`. `export["years"]` (a list of ints) and `export["rate"]` (text) are given.
**The snapshot** you build is the practice series' format, restricted to what this export carries:

A project started in year $`t`$ spends `cost[k]` in year $`t + k`$, so its start years are $`T_j = \{e_j, \dots, l_j\}`$, and every one of them must leave room for the whole profile inside the horizon.
In `export.py`, write the two stages (`review`, which runs them in order, and `rejected` are given). Each finding is a tuple `(severity, rule, subject)`.

rows: `(snapshot, [])` for clean cells; otherwise `(None, findings)` with **every** cell problem of every row
the findings of the three rules below, on a snapshot whose cells are clean

blocks.text: Cell rules (all errors). A budget row whose `year` is not a whole number (`"2O28"`) is a `bad-budget` with that text as its subject, and the year it was meant for then has no budget, so it also gets a `missing-budget`:

rows: a cost amount is not a whole number above 0 (one finding for the whole `cost` cell, however many of its amounts are bad), or `earliest`, `latest`, `lag`, `crews` is not a whole number
a program other than `lines`/`poles`, a region other than `North`/`South`, a `must` other than `0`/`1`

not $`y_0 \le e_j \le l_j`$ with $`l_j + n_j - 1 \le y_{\text{last}}`$, where $`n_j`$ is the number of amounts in the `cost` cell; checked whenever `earliest` and `latest` are whole numbers, even if an amount of `cost` is bad
the parent names no project of the export
its `year` or its `amount` is not a whole number, or the amount is below 0
a horizon year with no budget row that was read, unless a `bad-budget` finding already has that year as its subject
a second row with an id already read (that row is then skipped)
the ids on the cycle, sorted, joined with `+`
following parents from a project leads back to it
the parent's earliest start plus the lag is after the child's latest start
error for a must-do child, warning otherwise
the least that must-do work can spend in the year, each must-do at its cheapest start for that year, exceeds the year's budget

blocks.text: The cross rules read parents and costs as numbers and ids, so they run only once every cell is clean: an export with cell problems is refused on those alone, and its next version is checked again. Errors reject; a warning alone does not, and `review` then returns the snapshot. About seventy lines.

The practice simplifies the lesson's reader and gate: one cell rule, `not-a-number`, stands for the lesson's `not-a-whole-number` and `below-minimum`, and the gate has three rules instead of four (the lesson's `two-must-do-alternatives` is left out).

cases.says: a clean export is accepted, and its text cells become the practice snapshot's numbers, flags and ids
an export with six planted defects is rejected: the four cell defects first, then, once they are fixed, the two the cross-project rules find
a row with two bad cells reports both
a bad amount in the second year of a cost profile is found
a window whose last start leaves no room for the second year of work is empty
two projects that are each other's parent are one cycle, reported once
an optional child whose parent cannot start early enough still leaves a plan, so it only warns
the same problem on a must-do child proves there is no plan, so it blocks
a must-do that may start late spends nothing in an early year, so a small early budget is not an error
a budget row whose year is not a number is named by that text, and the year it was meant for is reported missing
a cost cell with a bad amount still has its length checked against the window
a cost cell with two bad amounts is one finding, not two

origin.section: Rules Across Projects Run Only on Clean Cells

concepts: an export reader that keeps every cell problem, and rules across projects that run only on clean cells, refusing an export with six planted defects
